title: [Classic Long-Form RPG] Does Perfectionism Make You Abandon Your Game? ① Player Edition

blocks.source: 【王道長編RPG】完璧主義はエターなる？① プレイヤー編
blocks.translation: [Classic Long-Form RPG] Does Perfectionism Make You Abandon Your Game? ① Player Edition

blocks.source: 制作中の作品で収集要素を実装するにあたり、『取り逃し要素』に関連して、ふと思ったことをつらつらと書いてみます。なんと、今回は心理学に挑戦です。
blocks.translation: As I implement collection elements in a game currently in development, I thought I would write down some thoughts related to “missable content.” And this time, I’m taking on psychology.

blocks.source: プレイヤーが取り逃しを嫌がる心理というのは、『完璧主義』という性格傾向で説明できるようです。どうやら、自分とズレの大きな人に共通するプレイスタイルを分析すると、この性格傾向が大きいのではないかと思い当たりました。というわけで、この完璧主義について色々と調べてみました。
blocks.translation: The psychology behind players disliking missable content seems to be explainable by the personality trait known as “perfectionism.” When I analyzed the play styles shared by people whose tendencies differ greatly from mine, I realized that this trait may be particularly strong among them. So, I looked into perfectionism in various ways.

blocks.source: ※注：以下はかなり突っ込んだ内容となります。結果的に完璧主義傾向がある人に対して、辛辣な内容も書いています。気分を害されるかもしれないので、あらかじめご了承ください。ただし、完璧主義の弊害に悩む人（特に作品を完成させられないエターナラー）にとって自分が伝えられることも書いたつもりです。
blocks.translation: ※Note: The following content goes into considerable depth. As a result, I have also written some harsh things about people with perfectionist tendencies. Please understand in advance that it may offend you. However, I have tried to include things I can convey to people troubled by the adverse effects of perfectionism (especially those who eternally abandon their games without ever finishing them).

blocks.source: 完璧主義なプレイヤー
blocks.translation: Perfectionist Players

blocks.source: 完璧主義／完璧主義者というのは完璧であろうとする性質や人のことです。そのまんまですね。『時間を守る』『納期を守る』『仕事は細部まで入念に仕上げる』『テストでは満点を目指す』といったタイプのようです。
blocks.translation: Perfectionism, or a perfectionist, refers to the quality of trying to be perfect, or to a person with that quality. It’s exactly what it sounds like. They seem to be the type who “is punctual,” “meets deadlines,” “meticulously finishes work down to the smallest details,” and “aims for perfect scores on tests.”

blocks.source: 努力家である反面、『細部にこだわって仕事が遅くなる』『与えられた枠組みにこだわるため柔軟性に欠ける』『完璧にできないことは投げ出す』というきらいがあるようです。
blocks.translation: Although they are hard workers, they also seem prone to “becoming slow at work because they obsess over details,” “lacking flexibility because they cling to the given framework,” and “giving up on anything they cannot do perfectly.”

blocks.source: ０か１００かの両極端な性格と言えるかもしれません。
blocks.translation: You might say they have an all-or-nothing personality.

blocks.source: 参考までに適当に見つけた性格診断の例です。
blocks.translation: For reference, here is an example of a personality test I found more or less at random.

blocks.source: http://shining.main.jp/enia1.html
blocks.translation: http://shining.main.jp/enia1.html

blocks.source: プラス面とマイナス面の内容がどう見ても矛盾してますが、これが両極端ということかもしれません。
blocks.translation: The positive and negative aspects seem completely contradictory, but perhaps that is what it means to be extreme.

blocks.source: １００問チェックでの診断もありますので、お暇でなおかつ「あたしってば完璧主義かも……」って人はどうぞ。下のタイプ１が完全主義者に当たりますので、ここのポイントで度合いが分かるかと思います。
blocks.translation: There is also a test consisting of 100 questions, so if you have time and think, “I might be a perfectionist…,” feel free to try it. Type 1 below corresponds to a perfectionist, so I think you can determine the degree from the score here.

blocks.source: http://shining.main.jp/eniatest.html
blocks.translation: http://shining.main.jp/eniatest.html

blocks.source: ちなみに、僕は１番目に研究者が９ポイント。２番目に完全主義者が６ポイントになりました。完璧主義傾向もなくはないですが、研究者のほうが遥かにしっくり来るので異論ありません。
blocks.translation: Incidentally, I scored 9 points as a researcher in first place, and 6 points as a perfectionist in second place. I do have some perfectionist tendencies, but “researcher” fits me far better, so I have no objections.

blocks.source: これがゲームのプレイスタイルにおいてはどうなるか。ググってみたら、出るわ出るわの完璧主義ゲーマーの実例。軽度な例から極端な例まで順番に挙げてみました。
blocks.translation: What does this look like in terms of gaming play styles? When I searched online, I found example after example of perfectionist gamers. I’ll list them in order, from mild to extreme.

blocks.source: ダンジョンは隅々まで歩いて、宝箱を回収。
blocks.translation: Walk through every corner of a dungeon and collect all the treasure chests.

blocks.source: 行き止まりに当たるとむしろ安心する。
blocks.translation: Actually feel relieved when reaching a dead end.

blocks.source: 期間限定要素などの取り逃しを嫌がる。攻略サイト見ながらプレイは当たり前。
blocks.translation: Dislike missing limited-time content and the like. Playing while looking at a walkthrough is a given.

blocks.source: クリア後の隠しボスもきっちり倒す。全イベントを見ようと努力。
blocks.translation: Defeat hidden bosses after clearing the game without fail. Make an effort to see every event.

blocks.source: お金、ＭＰ、消耗品、時間などのリソース活用は苦手。
blocks.translation: Be bad at managing resources such as money, MP, consumables, and time.

blocks.source: いらないアイテムを売って、お金に替えるというやり繰りは苦手。
blocks.translation: Be bad at making do by selling unwanted items for money.

blocks.source: エリクサーのような貴重品を使うなんてとんでもない。
blocks.translation: Using precious items like Elixirs is out of the question.

blocks.source: ブレスオブファイア５のようにリソース活用を強いられるシステムは発狂もの。
blocks.translation: Systems that force you to manage resources, like in Breath of Fire 5, are maddening.

blocks.source: 店売りの最強装備が全員分整うまで先に進まない。
blocks.translation: Do not proceed until the strongest equipment sold by the shop has been obtained for everyone.

blocks.source: 既にボスを余裕で倒せるレベルになっていてもとにかく整える。
blocks.translation: Get everything in order no matter what, even when already strong enough to defeat the boss with ease.

blocks.source: かかる時間も気にしない。
blocks.translation: Do not care how long it takes.

blocks.source: 戦闘に参加しないキャラまで整え出すとさらに高レベル。
blocks.translation: Be even more extreme when they start preparing equipment for characters who do not participate in battle.

blocks.source: 図鑑やアイテムは何の報酬もなくともコンプリートする。
blocks.translation: Complete the bestiary and item collection even without any reward.

blocks.source: 逃走回数や全滅回数のカウントがあると酷く気になる。
blocks.translation: Be terribly bothered when the number of times fled or wiped out is tracked.

blocks.source: 何かメリットがあるわけでもないが０を維持しようとする。
blocks.translation: Try to keep the count at 0 even though it provides no benefit.

blocks.source: 確率１％以下のレアアイテムを手に入れるまで、リセットを繰り返す。
blocks.translation: Keep resetting until obtaining a rare item with a drop rate of 1% or less.

blocks.source: レアであれば大した性能がなくとも関係なく取得対象。
blocks.translation: Anything rare becomes a target for acquisition, regardless of whether it has any significant usefulness.

blocks.source: 一つでも些細な何かを取り逃すと最初からやり直す。または投げ出す。
blocks.translation: Start over from the beginning—or give up—if they miss even one minor thing.

blocks.source: 上のほうに関しては普通のプレイヤーでも「あるある」だと思います。仲間を取り逃したなんてのは、僕でもやり直したくなります。幻想水滸伝なんて、仲間を揃えないとベストエンドにいけませんし。
blocks.translation: As for the items toward the top of the list, I think even ordinary players would say, “That’s so relatable.” Even I would want to start over if I missed a party member. In Suikoden, after all, you cannot reach the best ending unless you gather all the party members.

blocks.source: 完璧主義傾向というのは、どのプレイヤーも程度の差はあれど、持っているといえそうです。特にヘビーゲーマーで完璧主義傾向が全くないなんて人は極めて稀でしょう。
blocks.translation: It seems that every player has some degree of perfectionist tendencies. In particular, people who are heavy gamers yet have no perfectionist tendencies at all must be extremely rare.

blocks.source: さて、ここで問題が発生するのが下のほう。例えば、制作者が「必要な装備だけ買って先に進めば丁度よい」という調整をしていた場合、『５』のタイプのプレイヤーに対しては、その想定が崩れます。
blocks.translation: Now, the problem arises with the items toward the bottom. For example, if a creator balances the game so that “buying only the necessary equipment and proceeding is just right,” that assumption breaks down for type 5 players.

blocks.source: もっとも、プレイヤーが好きでやっている限りはそれほど大きな問題ではありません。想定したバランスでプレイしてもらえないのは残念、とはいえ「俺はガチガチに装備を整えて、無双するのが好きなんだ！」ってのも悪くない楽しみ方でしょう。
blocks.translation: Still, as long as the player is doing it because they enjoy it, it is not that major a problem. It is unfortunate if they do not play according to the intended balance, but “I like fully optimizing my equipment and steamrolling everything!” is not a bad way to enjoy a game either.

blocks.source: それだけならよかったのですが、話はそこに留まりません。完璧主義者の中には好きでやっているのではなく、『やらねばならない』という意識に縛られ、自ら疲れを買っている人がいるみたいです。
blocks.translation: That alone would have been fine, but the matter does not end there. Some perfectionists apparently are not doing these things because they enjoy them; instead, they are bound by the feeling that they “have to do it” and end up deliberately exhausting themselves.

blocks.source: 例えば、僕自身は実際に以下のような意見を受けたことがあります。
blocks.translation: For example, I have actually received opinions like the following.

blocks.source: プレイヤー
blocks.translation: Player

blocks.source: 「アイテムの値段が高い。全員分の装備を完璧に揃えるのが大変で疲れる」
blocks.translation: "The items are too expensive. It is difficult and exhausting to perfectly equip everyone."

blocks.source: 僕
blocks.translation: Me

blocks.source: 「えっ！？ 疲れるならなんで全部買うの！？
blocks.translation: "What!? If it’s exhausting, why buy everything?

blocks.source: 敵の強さで判断すれば、そこまでしなくても進めると分かるはず」
blocks.translation: You should be able to tell from the enemies’ strength that you can progress without going that far."

blocks.source: プレイヤー
blocks.translation: Player

blocks.source: 「戦歴に逃走回数が表示されるから、気になって逃走できない。
blocks.translation: "The number of times I’ve fled is displayed in the battle record, so it bothers me and I can’t run away.

blocks.source: 逃げずにプレイするのが面倒だ」
blocks.translation: Playing without fleeing is such a hassle."

blocks.source: 僕
blocks.translation: Me

blocks.source: 「逃げてもペナルティはないんですけど……。ていうか逃げてください」
blocks.translation: "There’s no penalty for fleeing, though… In fact, please do flee."

blocks.source: 「誰に強制されているわけでもないのに、やりたくないことをやる」という感覚が僕にはほとんど理解できませんでした。僕にしても宝箱やサブイベントの取り逃しぐらいは気にします。しかし、それも「アイテムが手に入る」「イベントが見れる」というご褒美あってのものです。
blocks.translation: I could hardly understand the feeling of “doing something you do not want to do even though no one is forcing you to.” Even I care about missing treasure chests and side events to some extent. However, that is because there is a reward involved: “getting an item” or “being able to see an event.”

blocks.source: 上記のようにご褒美のないことまで、完璧にする狙いは何でしょうか？ 上については「装備を整えて無双したい！」のかとも思いましたが、どうも違うように思います。そもそも、聞いてみると楽しいわけでもないようなので、ますます不可解です。
blocks.translation: What is the point of perfecting even things with no reward, as described above? Regarding the former, I thought perhaps it was “I want to fully equip myself and steamroll everything!” but it does not seem to be that. In the first place, when I ask them, it does not seem that they even enjoy it, which makes it increasingly puzzling.

blocks.source: 正直にいうと今までは「色んな人もいるもんだ」と流していました。色んな意見があるのは当然ですが、さりとて合わせていたらキリがありませんので。
blocks.translation: To be honest, until now I had simply brushed it off by thinking, “There are all kinds of people.” It is only natural for there to be all kinds of opinions, but if I tried to accommodate every one of them, there would be no end to it.

blocks.source: ですが、完璧主義者に関する記事を読んで、ようやく腑に落ちました。無関係だと思っていた複数の不可解な意見が『完璧主義』という線で一本に繋がったのです。この辺、結構自分はドライなほうなので、感覚が合わないはずです。
blocks.translation: However, after reading an article about perfectionists, it finally clicked. Several puzzling opinions that I had thought were unrelated were all connected by the thread of “perfectionism.” I’m actually rather detached in this regard, so I suppose our sensibilities wouldn’t align.

blocks.source: 察するに、完璧主義といっても『好きでやっているタイプ』と『強迫性でやっているタイプ』の二通りがいるのではないかと推測します。調べてみたら後者らしき人が「最近、ゲームを楽しめなくなった」「疲れるから、ＲＰＧは尻込みする」というようなことを、書いている例をいくつか見つけました。思っていた以上に重大そうです。
blocks.translation: Judging by this, I suspect there are two types of perfectionists: those who do it because they enjoy it, and those who do it compulsively. When I looked into it, I found several examples of people who seemed to be the latter writing things like, “I can’t enjoy games anymore” and “I shy away from RPGs because they’re exhausting.” It seems more serious than I had expected.

blocks.source: これ『心理学』や『ゲームデザイン』といった分野にとっては、論文一つ書いていいぐらいのテーマな気がします。
blocks.translation: For fields such as “psychology” and “game design,” this seems like a topic substantial enough to warrant writing an entire paper about.

blocks.source: ぶっちゃけ『強迫性』に陥っていて、楽しさよりもストレスが大きいという方は、無理に完璧を目指さないほうが、何かと幸せになれるのではないかと思ったり。少なくとも『本当に気に入った作品だけやり込む』『それ以外の作品は適当に』みたいな融通を利かせたほうがよいかと思います。色んなプレイスタイルがあってもよいとはいっても、楽しくないなら本末転倒です。
blocks.translation: To be frank, for those who have fallen into compulsive behavior and feel more stress than enjoyment, I sometimes think they would be happier in many ways if they stopped forcing themselves to aim for perfection. At the very least, I think it would be better to be flexible—for example, “only fully play the games you really love” and “take it easy with the rest.” There may be all kinds of playstyles, but if you aren’t having fun, that defeats the purpose.

blocks.source: あくまでプレイスタイルを決めるのは、当人の問題ではありますが、適度に自制し「ゲームを楽しめなくなった……」なんてことには、ならないで頂ければと切に願います。
blocks.translation: Ultimately, deciding on a playstyle is up to each individual, but I sincerely hope that you exercise reasonable restraint and don’t end up thinking, “I can’t enjoy games anymore……”

blocks.source: では制作者側に何ができるかというと、何よりも取り逃し要素を減らすことでしょう。これについては、大半のユーザが意見一致すると思います。もちろん、一周が短く、周回プレイが前提なら、取り逃しがあるくらいのほうがやりがいが出るというのは否定しません。
blocks.translation: As for what developers can do, the most important thing would be to reduce missable content. I think most users would agree on this. Of course, if one playthrough is short and replaying is expected, I won’t deny that having some missable content can make the game more rewarding.

blocks.source: その他については、もう作者のお好みでよいかなと思います。というのも、仮説が正しければ、上の２タイプは正反対の心理反応を取るはずです。
blocks.translation: As for everything else, I think it’s fine to leave it to the author’s preference. After all, if the hypothesis is correct, the two types above should have completely opposite psychological reactions.

blocks.source: 例：魔物図鑑を用意した場合
blocks.translation: Example: If You Include a Monster Encyclopedia

blocks.source: 『好きでやっているタイプ』→ よ～しコンプするぞ！
blocks.translation: "The type who does it because they enjoy it” → All right, I’m going to complete it!

blocks.source: 『強迫性タイプ』 → げっ、コンプしないと……。
blocks.translation: "The compulsive type” → Oh no, I have to complete it……

blocks.source: そんなわけで、両方を満足させるというのは相当難しいはずです。ぶっちゃけ僕もこれ以上はどうすりゃいいのかよく分かりません。今後の課題というところですね。
blocks.translation: So, satisfying both types must be extremely difficult. To be honest, I don’t really know what else I could do about it, either. I suppose it’s an issue for the future.

blocks.source: ……うん。ロクな結論は出ませんでした。それでも意識だけしておけばその内、役に立つ時も来るかもしれません。
blocks.translation: ……Yeah. I didn’t arrive at any particularly useful conclusion. Still, if you keep it in mind, it might prove useful someday.

blocks.source: ※長すぎたので分割しました。
blocks.translation: ※It was too long, so I split it up.

In Suikoden, after all, you cannot reach the best ending unless you gather all the party members.
texts.完璧主義傾向というのは、どのプレイヤーも程度の差はあれど、持っているといえそうで: It seems that every player has some degree of perfectionist tendencies. In particular, people who are heavy gamers yet have no perfectionist tendencies at all must be extremely rare.
texts.さて、ここで問題が発生するのが下のほう。例えば、制作者が「必要な装備だけ買って先: Now, the problem arises with the items toward the bottom. For example, if a creator balances the game so that “buying only the necessary equipment and proceeding is just right,” that assumption breaks down for type 5 players.
texts.もっとも、プレイヤーが好きでやっている限りはそれほど大きな問題ではありません。想: Still, as long as the player is doing it because they enjoy it, it is not that major a problem. It is unfortunate if they do not play according to the intended balance, but “I like fully optimizing my equipment and steamrolling everything!” is not a bad way to enjoy a game either.
texts.それだけならよかったのですが、話はそこに留まりません。完璧主義者の中には好きでや: That alone would have been fine, but the matter does not end there. Some perfectionists apparently are not doing these things because they enjoy them; instead, they are bound by the feeling that they “have to do it” and end up deliberately exhausting themselves.

texts.「逃げてもペナルティはないんですけど……。ていうか逃げてください」: "There’s no penalty for fleeing, though… In fact, please do flee."
texts.「誰に強制されているわけでもないのに、やりたくないことをやる」という感覚が僕には: I could hardly understand the feeling of “doing something you do not want to do even though no one is forcing you to.” Even I care about missing treasure chests and side events to some extent. However, that is because there is a reward involved: “getting an item” or “being able to see an event.”
texts.上記のようにご褒美のないことまで、完璧にする狙いは何でしょうか？ 上については「: What is the point of perfecting even things with no reward, as described above? Regarding the former, I thought perhaps it was “I want to fully equip myself and steamroll everything!” but it does not seem to be that. In the first place, when I ask them, it does not seem that they even enjoy it, which makes it increasingly puzzling.
texts.正直にいうと今までは「色んな人もいるもんだ」と流していました。色んな意見があるの: To be honest, until now I had simply brushed it off by thinking, “There are all kinds of people.” It is only natural for there to be all kinds of opinions, but if I tried to accommodate every one of them, there would be no end to it.
texts.ですが、完璧主義者に関する記事を読んで、ようやく腑に落ちました。無関係だと思って: However, after reading an article about perfectionists, it finally clicked. Several puzzling opinions that I had thought were unrelated were all connected by the thread of “perfectionism.” I’m actually rather detached in this regard, so I suppose our sensibilities wouldn’t align.
texts.察するに、完璧主義といっても『好きでやっているタイプ』と『強迫性でやっているタイ: Judging by this, I suspect there are two types of perfectionists: those who do it because they enjoy it, and those who do it compulsively. When I looked into it, I found several examples of people who seemed to be the latter writing things like, “I can’t enjoy games anymore” and “I shy away from RPGs because they’re exhausting.” It seems more serious than I had expected.
texts.これ『心理学』や『ゲームデザイン』といった分野にとっては、論文一つ書いていいぐら: For fields such as “psychology” and “game design,” this seems like a topic substantial enough to warrant writing an entire paper about.
texts.ぶっちゃけ『強迫性』に陥っていて、楽しさよりもストレスが大きいという方は、無理に: To be frank, for those who have fallen into compulsive behavior and feel more stress than enjoyment, I sometimes think they would be happier in many ways if they stopped forcing themselves to aim for perfection. At the very least, I think it would be better to be flexible—for example, “only fully play the games you really love” and “take it easy with the rest.” There may be all kinds of playstyles, but if you aren’t having fun, that defeats the purpose.
texts.あくまでプレイスタイルを決めるのは、当人の問題ではありますが、適度に自制し「ゲー: Ultimately, deciding on a playstyle is up to each individual, but I sincerely hope that you exercise reasonable restraint and don’t end up thinking, “I can’t enjoy games anymore……”
texts.では制作者側に何ができるかというと、何よりも取り逃し要素を減らすことでしょう。こ: As for what developers can do, the most important thing would be to reduce missable content. I think most users would agree on this. Of course, if one playthrough is short and replaying is expected, I won’t deny that having some missable content can make the game more rewarding.
texts.その他については、もう作者のお好みでよいかなと思います。というのも、仮説が正しけ: As for everything else, I think it’s fine to leave it to the author’s preference. After all, if the hypothesis is correct, the two types above should have completely opposite psychological reactions.
